column1: # P20: the models each VRAM tier is measured on, every engine on the same GPU (scripts/consumer_bench.sh; benchmarks/consumer/README.md).
# tier_gb: the GPU memory class the row is measured on (8, 12, 16, 24 or 32). model: the Hub repo (its family's current release; released: its date).
# params_b: its parameters, in billions, as `glyd fit` counts them (which model is the largest, and a GGUF's bits a weight). glyd: the level Glyd runs it at. gguf: the llama.cpp quant of the same
# weights at about the same bits, QUANT or QUANT@REPO where it is made from another checkpoint of the model (Google's QAT one for gemma's wren);
# the same GGUF file is what Ollama and LM Studio are given. A row's gguf "-" has no llama.cpp side.
# A row is a model at a level that `glyd fit` loads on a card of its tier: a mixture of experts may keep experts in the computer's memory (the
# script takes that step); a dense model has to fit the card. On 16 GB (v0.35.0, RTX 4080 SUPER, 28 GiB of memory for the run): Nemotron 3.5
# Lightning loads at wren and not at kestrel (28.2 GiB of the computer's memory); Qwen3.8-27B at no level (wren takes 16.6 GiB of the card).
